title: MSO Foundations
summary: The foundations: what tokens and the context window are, why the same prompt can give different answers, how model choice and reasoning modes trade quality against speed and cost, how much to show Claude by example, and the ways your code talks to the API.

takeaways.title: Tokens are the unit of input, output and cost.
takeaways.body: Think and budget in tokens rather than words, since that is what the API meters and what the context window measures.

takeaways.title: The context window is a fixed token budget that holds the whole request at once.
takeaways.body: An oversized input errors before generation, while hitting the ceiling mid-generation returns truncated output with a `model_context_window_exceeded` stop reason, so managing history is the application's job.

takeaways.title: Sampling makes generation non-deterministic.
takeaways.body: The same prompt can return different wording on each run, so testing on exact text is unreliable. This is what evals are built for.

takeaways.title: Model choice and reasoning mode are separate, composable levers.
takeaways.body: Pick the smallest model and the simplest reasoning and prompting that meet your eval, and add capability only where the eval says you need it.

takeaways.title: A developer reaches Claude over a REST API, usually through an SDK.
takeaways.body: Choose between synchronous, streaming, async/await or batch based on whether a user is waiting and whether the workload is real-time or bulk offline.

title: Production-Grade Prompting, Agents & Tool Use
summary: The craft of a production app: getting reliable structured output, deciding when Claude should think, designing tools Claude picks correctly (or borrowing them over MCP), handling streams safely, keeping context in budget, wiring an agent and its memory, and choosing the right API for bulk and multimodal work.

modules.title: The three places a RAG path breaks

takeaways.title: When a prompt fails, the failure type tells you which technique is missing.
takeaways.body: Unparseable or malformed output points to structured outputs; inconsistent format points to examples; weak multi-step reasoning points to thinking. Diagnose the failure before rewriting the prompt.

takeaways.title: Match the reasoning depth to the task before you tune the prompt.
takeaways.body: Set thinking and effort to fit the task first, then add prompt guidance only where results still fall short. And when thinking blocks are in the conversation, send them back unchanged.

takeaways.title: A stream ending is not a message completing.
takeaways.body: Act on a block only after its `content_block_stop`, read the final `stop_reason` from `message_delta`, and if the stream is cut off, never save the partial assistant turn as if it were a finished reply.

takeaways.title: Every wrong-tool selection traces back to the schema, and most of the time to the description.
takeaways.body: Claude chooses tools from their name, description and `input_schema`. When it picks the wrong one, check for vague or overlapping descriptions first.

takeaways.title: Context is a fixed budget, and tool outputs spend it faster than anything else in the loop.
takeaways.body: Keep low-signal output out at the source, clear or compact what is no longer needed, hand big searches to subagents, and use prompt caching and token counting to control cost and headroom.

takeaways.title: The workflow-or-agent decision sets the cost of everything that follows, and human checkpoints belong in the design.
takeaways.body: Use a predefined workflow when the steps are known and an agent only when the path can't be scripted. Plan where a human approves risky actions up front, not as an afterthought.

takeaways.title: Memory scope is decided by the shape of the session, not by what is easiest to implement.
takeaways.body: Single-session tasks can live in context; work that spans sessions needs external storage or summaries; reusable know-how belongs in Skills that load only when needed.

takeaways.title: Calculate the cost of a multimodal input before you write the ingestion code, and match the API to the workload.
takeaways.body: Estimate image and PDF tokens up front. Bulk jobs nobody is waiting on belong in the Message Batches API; looping over the synchronous API is not batching.

title: Claude Code, MCP & Integration
summary: Running Claude Code safely and sharing the setup: choosing a permission mode and placing the human gate, giving every session durable context, packaging workflows as skills, commands and plugins, configuring MCP servers by transport and scope, and authenticating to enterprise systems without leaking secrets.

modules.title: Packaging workflows: skills, commands and plugins

takeaways.title: Permission mode is a risk decision, not a speed decision.
takeaways.body: Pick the mode by the worst thing that could happen in this environment. Prompts cost time on trusted work, but bypassing them on a machine with live files removes every safety check between the agent and those files.

takeaways.title: An AI code review gives you a set of findings to triage, not a verdict to apply.
takeaways.body: Treat each finding as a claim to check: confirm it, fix what is real, and dismiss what is not. A human still decides what merges.

takeaways.title: A skill is portable, but "runs everywhere" is something you design for.
takeaways.body: Write the description as the matching criterion, don't assume a local filesystem or local tools inside the skill, and remember that a subagent doesn't inherit the skills you used in the main session: preload what it needs with its `skills` field.

takeaways.title: Durable context requires the right mechanism for each concern.
takeaways.body: Universal constraints go in CLAUDE.md, path-specific guidance in scoped rules files, rules that must never be broken in hooks, on-demand know-how in skills, and isolated side work in subagents.

takeaways.title: A shareable setup requires portable components.
takeaways.body: Bundle skills, commands, hooks, subagents and MCP servers as a plugin so a team installs one unit, and keep machine-specific paths and secrets out of what you share.

takeaways.title: Transport and scope are independent decisions with dependent consequences.
takeaways.body: Transport is how Claude Code talks to a server (stdio locally, HTTP remotely); scope is who loads it (local, project or user, with managed configuration on top for the organization). A project-scoped server is shared with everyone on the repo, so its transport and credentials must work for all of them.

takeaways.title: Enterprise integration requires identifying the security requirements before deployment.
takeaways.body: Match authentication to the service type, keep credentials out of configuration and rotate them, and settle blast radius, audit logging and phase approvals before an agent touches high-risk systems.

title: Production Engineering, Evals & Security
summary: Taking a Claude feature to production: defining done with evals and a calibrated judge, testing at the right level and tracing failures to their step, sorting errors into retriable and terminal, choosing and routing models, keeping cost and latency in budget across agents, and defending against prompt injection with enforced boundaries.

takeaways.title: Set the standard before you build it.
takeaways.body: Write down what done, safe and affordable mean, then turn it into an eval: input cases, expected behaviors and a grader matched to the output's shape. Calibrate any LLM judge against human grades before trusting its scores.

takeaways.title: Match the test to the failure, and trace so you know where it happened.
takeaways.body: Unit, functional, integration and end-to-end tests each catch a failure the others miss. Test the shape of Claude's output rather than its exact text, and keep a trace of each step so a bad result points to the step that produced it.

takeaways.title: Sort every failure, then handle them individually.
takeaways.body: Ask whether waiting and resending the same request could work. Retry what is retriable with backoff, and know what the SDK already retries; fix what is terminal instead of retrying it. When a tool fails, tell Claude with `is_error` rather than returning an empty result.

takeaways.title: Measure cost and latency per call, and fan out only when a task truly splits.
takeaways.body: Track tokens, latency and errors for every call so you can find the step that drives the bill. Use the levers that fit (model choice, context size, caching, batching) and treat multi-agent orchestration as a trade of many more tokens for parallelism.

takeaways.title: Treat fetched content as data and enforce the boundary with a hook.
takeaways.body: Anything the agent didn't write can carry injected instructions. Keep it separate from trusted instructions, give tools least privilege, block sensitive actions with hooks that run regardless of what the model was told, and keep sandboxing as the backstop.

title: Accelerators and IP Contribution
summary: Turning a finished build into an asset: packaging it so the next engagement starts from a working foundation, contributing it back through the right channel, carrying requirements through the lifecycle, choosing where a Claude workload runs and pinning what ships, comparing platforms on the dimension that decides, and holding trust boundaries across connected components.

takeaways.title: Package while the build is fresh.
takeaways.body: Separate what is customer-specific from what is reusable while you still remember why each choice was made. Expose the customer-specific parts as parameters with documented defaults, and ship the assumptions, the eval suite and the audit logging with the code.

takeaways.title: A maintainer accepts what they can verify.
takeaways.body: Send a contribution through the channel built for it, settle rights and attribution before asking for technical review, and make its behavior checkable: tests, clear docs, disclosed data flows and no secrets.

takeaways.title: Pin what ships.
takeaways.body: Ship a specific model version so an upstream change can't silently change production, and plan migrations anyway, because pinned versions still retire. Re-run your evals before you move.

takeaways.title: Measure the dimension that decides the placement.
takeaways.body: The customer's cloud, identity and compliance needs usually narrow the platform first. Then measure what still decides it, such as latency from the customer's region with realistic prompts, or the total cost beyond the per-token rate.

takeaways.title: Mark every seam as a boundary.
takeaways.body: Map which component does what before connecting them. Wherever data moves between components, treat what crosses as untrusted until checked, and give each component only the access its own job needs.
